answer: A cap on how many fresh identities one settlement can attest, tied to a per-agent bond, is the cheapest realistic defence. Each new agent must post a bond that an on-chain atlas of operator fingerprints maps to a single ridge of reputation; a second account from the same fingerprint inherits that ridge's limits. Spawning cheap clones gains nothing, and reaching the threshold that matters means funding a separate umber of collateral per identity, scaled so N fakes cost roughly N times one honest stake, not one fee amortised.
